balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

feeIncome.title: Fee and commission income
feeIncome.content:
Fee & commission income is brokerage commissions, investment-banking (underwriting/advisory) fees and asset-management fees -- the capital-light, scale-sensitive half of a securities firm's revenue, as distinct from net interest and trading/investment income which depend on balance-sheet size and market direction.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): this line nearly doubled in FY2025 (RMB38.6bn vs RMB21.1bn in FY2024) as mainland trading turnover surged and the Haitong merger added scale; H1 FY2026's RMB25.1bn is already ahead of all of FY2024.

What to watch:

  • Whether growth is turnover-driven (cyclical) or market-share-driven (structural)
  • IB fee income specifically, which depends on the new-listing and bond-underwriting pipeline

marginBook.title: Margin accounts receivable
marginBook.content:
Margin accounts receivable is the amount clients owe the broker for margin-financed share purchases -- the broker's own lending book, funded mostly by the broker's balance sheet and client collateral.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): the book roughly tripled from RMB106bn (FY2024) to RMB254bn (FY2025) to RMB299bn (H1 FY2026), tracking the mainland A-share rally and the Haitong merger's combined client base. It is both a growth driver (net interest income) and a risk exposure (forced-selling losses if the market falls sharply).

What to watch:

  • Growth outpacing the broader market (share gain) versus simply tracking it (beta)
  • Collateral coverage ratios in a market downturn -- not disclosed in these filings but the key risk

revenueVsTotalIncome.title: Core revenue vs total revenue and other income
revenueVsTotalIncome.content:
Revenue (core) is operating revenue from brokerage, margin financing, investment banking and asset management. Total revenue & other income adds items such as investment gains, government grants and (in FY2025) a large one-off gain.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): FY2025's gap (RMB104bn total vs RMB94bn core Revenue) is dominated by the bargain-purchase gain recognised on the Haitong Securities absorption merger -- an accounting gain from acquiring net assets below their fair value, not repeatable operating income. Strip it out before extrapolating FY2025 profitability forward.

What to watch:

  • The gap narrowing back toward historical levels (FY2018-FY2024 ran RMB5-10bn wide) once the merger gain rolls off
  • Whether post-merger core Revenue growth holds up without the one-off

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Guotai Haitong Securities Co., Ltd. (formerly Guotai Junan Securities): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
